1	# poly
2	
3	**A programming language and runtime for the stateful core of software written by coding agents.**
4	
5	A poly program is a set of declared state machines. Each machine carries its contract, its invariants, its effects and the obligations that govern it. The compiler checks the program exhaustively over declared finite domains before it may run. The runtime executes the same program durably, gates every effect, and writes a ledger that replays exactly.
6	
7	poly adds no new checking, simulation or governance engine. It is a compiler, a toolchain and one runtime integration over the Poly stack. Every construct lowers to an artefact an existing engine already reads:
8	
9	| Stage | Engines |
10	|---|---|
11	| Model and check | SAM v2, polygraph, polyrun, polyvers, polynv |
12	| Govern | Polyaxion, polycheck |
13	| Workflows | polyflow, polycrew |
14	| Learn | Polyx, polyness |
15	| Simulate (v2) | Polytrion |
16	
17	> Status: specification, draft v0.6 (after five reviews). No code yet.
18	
19	## Hello, world
20	
21	A turnstile. Put a coin in, it unlocks; push it, it locks.
22	
23	```poly
24	module hello
25	
26	type Mode = Locked | Unlocked
27	
28	machine Gate {
29	  state {
30	    mode  : Mode = Locked
31	    coins : 0..3 = 0
32	  }
33	  action Coin()
34	  action Push()
35	
36	  on Coin {
37	    require coins < 3 else reject "coin-box-full"
38	    coins' = coins + 1
39	    mode' = Unlocked
40	  }
41	  on Push {
42	    require mode is Unlocked else reject "locked"
43	    mode' = Locked
44	  }
45	
46	  invariant locked-when-empty: coins == 0 implies mode is Locked
47	}
48	```
49	
50	```
51	$ poly check hello.poly
52	hello.poly:5  PL3201 DEADLOCK  Gate
53	  no action is accepted in a reachable non-terminal state
54	  witness (4 steps):
55	    Coin()   Locked/0   -> Unlocked/1
56	    Coin()   Unlocked/1 -> Unlocked/2
57	    Coin()   Unlocked/2 -> Unlocked/3
58	    Push()   Unlocked/3 -> Locked/3      then Coin: coin-box-full, Push: locked
59	verdict: FINDINGS (exit 1)  over coins ∈ 0..3; 7 states
60	```
61	
62	The invariant holds. What `poly check` finds is that a full coin box locks the turnstile forever. Add an operator action and it is clean:
63	
64	```poly
65	  action Empty()
66	  on Empty {
67	    require mode is Locked else reject "unlocked"
68	    coins' = 0
69	  }
70	```
71	
72	Running it from TypeScript takes three lines:
73	
74	```ts
75	const rt = await load('./.poly/build')
76	const gate = await rt.create('hello.Gate')
77	await rt.dispatch(gate.id, 'Coin', {}, { actionId: 'coin-1' })   // { stepKind: 'accepted', state: { mode: 'Unlocked', coins: 1 } }
78	```
79	
80	Handlers are pure functions of the pre-state: a primed field is written, never read. That is why the order of lines inside a handler cannot change what it does. The same machine can also be written as TypeScript with the embedded surface (technical specification, PT2.5).
81	
82	## A second look: the double charge
83	
84	```poly
85	machine Order {
86	  state {
87	    status : Status = Draft
88	    items  : 0..3   = 0
89	    paid   : bool   = false
90	  }
91	  action AddItem()
92	  action Place()
93	  action Pay(amount: int check { 10, 20 })
94	
95	  on Place {
96	    require status == Draft else reject "not-draft"
97	    require items > 0      else reject "empty-order"
98	    status' = Placed
99	  }
100	  on Pay(amount) {
101	    require status == Placed else reject "not-placed"
102	    emit charge(amount)
103	  }
104	
105	  invariant shipped-was-paid: status == Shipped implies paid
106	  path property charge-at-most-once: count("payment.charge") <= 1
107	
108	  effect charge(amount: int) {
109	    kind "payment.charge"
110	    labels { egress:external }
111	    class irreversible
112	    ok -> PaymentOk()
113	    failed -> PaymentFailed(code: "declined")
114	  }
115	}
116	```
117	
118	`poly check` finds that two `Pay` calls emit two charges, and says why they can:
119	
120	```
121	orders.poly:17  PL4001 PATH_PROPERTY  charge-at-most-once
122	  witness (4 steps):
123	    AddItem()      Draft/0  -> Draft/1
124	    Place()        Draft/1  -> Placed/1
125	    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
126	    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge   <- count = 2
127	  test:  poly witness sha256:3be1… --test   (fails on this program)
128	  fixes: [enter-charging-status]  add status Charging, entered by Pay, left by PaymentOk / PaymentFailed
129	orders.poly:16  PL4002 EMIT_WITHOUT_STATE_CHANGE  Pay
130	  Pay emits payment.charge and leaves the state unchanged, so it can repeat its effect without limit
131	  witness (4 steps):
132	    AddItem()      Draft/0  -> Draft/1
133	    Place()        Draft/1  -> Placed/1
134	    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
135	    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
136	  fixes: [enter-charging-status]  record the emission in the state
137	verdict: FINDINGS (exit 1)  over items ∈ 0..3, amount ∈ {10, 20}
138	```
139	
140	Each call is allowed; the sequence is not. The second finding names the cause: a step that emits and changes nothing can always be taken again. That is the bug the Poly stack was built to find, reported before the program can run. The snippet is abridged; the full example is in the technical specification, PT4.5.
141	
142	
143	
144	## A third look: machines that talk
145	
146	Machines hold addresses, not each other's state, and talk only by `send`. A **configuration** checks several of them together, with messages arriving in any order. In the checkout example (technical specification, PT7a), an inventory and each order are safe on their own. If the order confirms as soon as it hears "available", two orders can both be confirmed against the last unit:
147	
148	```
149	checkout.poly:33  PL5401 CONFIGURATION_INVARIANT  confirmed-within-stock
150	  witness: Place@order[0], Place@order[1], Query(order[0]) -> inv, Query(order[1]) -> inv,
151	           Available(1) -> order[0], Available(1) -> order[1]
152	```
153	
154	No per-machine check can see this. The defect lives in the arrival order between machines.

174	
175	## Principles
176	
177	0. **The semantics is the definition.** 04-semantics says what a program means; every `poly check` validates the lowering against it.
178	0a. **One program, three interpreters.** The same machine is checked (all inputs), simulated (sampled inputs, v2) and run (real inputs). Only the environment changes.
179	0b. **Machines talk only by messages.** Addresses are values, `send` is the only way to affect a peer, and interacting machines are checked together as configurations.
180	1. **The engines check single machines; poly checks how machines relate.** Safety, governance, simulation and mining stay in the engines. poly's own model checker, poly-ref, checks the lowering, deadlock, liveness and configurations.
181	2. **The checked program is the running program, over its check domains.** A certificate binds the source, the artefacts and the check results by digest. Out-of-domain inputs are rejected (`strict`) or journaled as drift (`disclosed`).
182	3. **One source per machine.** Every engine artefact is derived.
183	4. **No silent clean.** Every check reports clean, findings, refused, underpowered or inconclusive.
184	5. **No model call on a check or decision path.**
185	6. **The journal is the corpus.** Runtime journals feed replay, versioning, mining and simulation unchanged.
186	
187	## Conclusion
188	
189	The Poly stack already holds the primitives a coding agent needs to write stateful code that holds. poly makes them one language. The first milestone is a lowering that reproduces the field-study results from poly source. The third is an experiment, run before any runtime is built, that measures escaped defects and cost against the host language alone. The runtime work depends on its result.
190	
191	## Glossary
192	
193	| Term | Meaning |
194	|---|---|
195	| **SAM** | State-Action-Model. The pattern every poly machine lowers to, in its v2 strict profile. |
196	| **Machine** | A sealed state, a set of actions and one handler per action. The unit of checking and of execution. |
197	| **Handler** | `on Action { … }`. Requires first, then writes. It either accepts or rejects with a named reason. |
198	| **Check domain** | The finite set of values a field or parameter takes during checking. Narrower than the runtime type when declared so, and then disclosed. |
199	| **Invariant** | A predicate on states that holds in every reachable state. |
200	| **Step property** | A predicate on every accepted step `(pre, action, data, post)`. |
201	| **Reject property** | A predicate on every step, whatever its verdict. |
202	| **Path property** | A prefix-closed predicate on the effects emitted along a path, such as `count(k) <= 1`. |
203	| **Liveness** | A property that something eventually happens, stated with the weak-fairness assumption it needs; its counterexample is a lasso. |
204	| **Deadlock** | A reachable non-terminal state in which no action is accepted. Checked for every machine. |
205	| **Checked instance** | The finite set of inputs and states a verdict covers. Every verdict is printed with it. |
206	| **poly-ref** | poly's model checker: a reference interpreter written from 04-semantics, used for translation validation, deadlock, liveness, configurations and obligation consistency. |
207	| **Possibility property** | A property that a good path exists (such as a mandate being dischargeable), as opposed to a property of all behaviours. |
208	| **Trust scope** | The governance scope an instance belongs to. Messages that cross a trust scope pass the gate. |
209	| **Tagged union** | A type whose values are one of several constructors, each with its own payload. Makes invalid states unrepresentable. |
210	| **Tri** | The three-valued truth type of policy expressions (true, false, unknown). Machine expressions are `Bool`. |
211	| **Capability** | An object passed to a handler that grants exactly the authority its effect's labels and targets declare. |
212	| **Interpretation** | One of three ways to feed the same machine: check (all inputs), simulate (sampled inputs) or run (real inputs). |
213	| **Embedded surface** | poly written as valid TypeScript with the `poly/embed` combinators; it produces the same AST as the standalone syntax. |
214	| **Ref** | The address of an instance (`Ref<M>`). It can be stored and passed in messages, but not dereferenced. |
215	| **Configuration** | A finite set of instances checked together, with messages in transit delivered in any order within a declared bound. |
216	| **Attached / detached child** | An attached child shares its parent's atomic cascade and kernel shard. A detached child is a separate actor that communicates by messages. |
217	| **Delivery guarantee** | Every message sent is eventually received: part of the semantics, implemented by the runtime (obligation R1). |
218	| **Dischargeable** | A mandate is dischargeable when some path reaches its discharge state without a deny under all obligations together. |
219	| **Kernel assumption** | A property of the runtime (K1 to K8) that a guarantee about running programs depends on. |
220	| **Witness** | The shortest concrete sequence that violates an invariant or reaches a forbidden region. It can be exported as a trace and as a test. |
221	| **Effect** | A declared side effect emitted by an accepted step. It carries labels and a class, and passes the gate before it runs. |
222	| **Label** | A term from a closed vocabulary (for example `egress:external`) that describes what an effect touches. |
223	| **Obligation** | A rule, machine, invariant or recalled text inside a `policy`, enforced by the Polyaxion gate. |
224	| **Effect gate** | The Polyaxion guarded merge that decides allow, deny or escalate before an effect or tool call executes. Distinct from the polycheck runtime guard and the polygents gate. |
225	| **Strict / disclosed** | The two modes of a check domain. `strict` rejects out-of-domain input at dispatch; `disclosed` accepts it and journals it as drift. |
226	| **Admission** | Passing the check pipeline. Only admitted programs load. |
227	| **Certificate** | The signed record of what was checked: source digest, artefact digests, check results, domains, stages not run and accepted exceptions. |
228	| **Ledger** | The signed record of steps, proposals, verdicts, effects, observations and advice, hash-chained per run. |
229	| **Anchor** | A signed Merkle root over the heads of all runs, published periodically, proving no run was dropped from a period. |
230	| **Work order** | An effect of a workflow machine, handed to an agent or a person to claim, run and report. |
231	| **World** | A set of machines, responders and drivers that Polytrion runs against a virtual clock. Deferred to v2. |
232	| **Lowering** | Compiling a poly construct into the artefact an existing engine reads. |

A poly program is a set of declared state machines. Each machine carries its contract, its invariants, its effects and the obligations that govern it. The compiler checks the program exhaustively over declared finite domains before it may run. The runtime executes the same program durably, gates every effect, and writes a ledger that replays exactly.

poly adds no new checking, simulation or governance engine. It is a compiler, a toolchain and one runtime integration over the Poly stack. Every construct lowers to an artefact an existing engine already reads:

| Stage | Engines |
|---|---|
| Model and check | SAM v2, polygraph, polyrun, polyvers, polynv |
| Govern | Polyaxion, polycheck |
| Workflows | polyflow, polycrew |
| Learn | Polyx, polyness |
| Simulate (v2) | Polytrion |

## Hello, world

A turnstile. Put a coin in, it unlocks; push it, it locks.

```poly
module hello

type Mode = Locked | Unlocked

machine Gate {
  state {
    mode  : Mode = Locked
    coins : 0..3 = 0
  }
  action Coin()
  action Push()

  on Coin {
    require coins < 3 else reject "coin-box-full"
    coins' = coins + 1
    mode' = Unlocked
  }
  on Push {
    require mode is Unlocked else reject "locked"
    mode' = Locked
  }

  invariant locked-when-empty: coins == 0 implies mode is Locked
}
```

```
$ poly check hello.poly
hello.poly:5  PL3201 DEADLOCK  Gate
  no action is accepted in a reachable non-terminal state
  witness (4 steps):
    Coin()   Locked/0   -> Unlocked/1
    Coin()   Unlocked/1 -> Unlocked/2
    Coin()   Unlocked/2 -> Unlocked/3
    Push()   Unlocked/3 -> Locked/3      then Coin: coin-box-full, Push: locked
verdict: FINDINGS (exit 1)  over coins ∈ 0..3; 7 states
```

The invariant holds. What `poly check` finds is that a full coin box locks the turnstile forever. Add an operator action and it is clean:

```poly
  action Empty()
  on Empty {
    require mode is Locked else reject "unlocked"
    coins' = 0
  }
```

Running it from TypeScript takes three lines:

```ts
const rt = await load('./.poly/build')
const gate = await rt.create('hello.Gate')
await rt.dispatch(gate.id, 'Coin', {}, { actionId: 'coin-1' })   // { stepKind: 'accepted', state: { mode: 'Unlocked', coins: 1 } }
```

Handlers are pure functions of the pre-state: a primed field is written, never read. That is why the order of lines inside a handler cannot change what it does. The same machine can also be written as TypeScript with the embedded surface (technical specification, PT2.5).

## A second look: the double charge

```poly
machine Order {
  state {
    status : Status = Draft
    items  : 0..3   = 0
    paid   : bool   = false
  }
  action AddItem()
  action Place()
  action Pay(amount: int check { 10, 20 })

  on Place {
    require status == Draft else reject "not-draft"
    require items > 0      else reject "empty-order"
    status' = Placed
  }
  on Pay(amount) {
    require status == Placed else reject "not-placed"
    emit charge(amount)
  }

  invariant shipped-was-paid: status == Shipped implies paid
  path property charge-at-most-once: count("payment.charge") <= 1

  effect charge(amount: int) {
    kind "payment.charge"
    labels { egress:external }
    class irreversible
    ok -> PaymentOk()
    failed -> PaymentFailed(code: "declined")
  }
}
```

`poly check` finds that two `Pay` calls emit two charges, and says why they can:

```
orders.poly:17  PL4001 PATH_PROPERTY  charge-at-most-once
  witness (4 steps):
    AddItem()      Draft/0  -> Draft/1
    Place()        Draft/1  -> Placed/1
    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge   <- count = 2
  test:  poly witness sha256:3be1… --test   (fails on this program)
  fixes: [enter-charging-status]  add status Charging, entered by Pay, left by PaymentOk / PaymentFailed
orders.poly:16  PL4002 EMIT_WITHOUT_STATE_CHANGE  Pay
  Pay emits payment.charge and leaves the state unchanged, so it can repeat its effect without limit
  witness (4 steps):
    AddItem()      Draft/0  -> Draft/1
    Place()        Draft/1  -> Placed/1
    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
    Pay(10)        Placed/1 -> Placed/1   emits payment.charge
  fixes: [enter-charging-status]  record the emission in the state
verdict: FINDINGS (exit 1)  over items ∈ 0..3, amount ∈ {10, 20}
```

Each call is allowed; the sequence is not. The second finding names the cause: a step that emits and changes nothing can always be taken again. That is the bug the Poly stack was built to find, reported before the program can run. The snippet is abridged; the full example is in the technical specification, PT4.5.



## A third look: machines that talk

Machines hold addresses, not each other's state, and talk only by `send`. A **configuration** checks several of them together, with messages arriving in any order. In the checkout example (technical specification, PT7a), an inventory and each order are safe on their own. If the order confirms as soon as it hears "available", two orders can both be confirmed against the last unit:

```
checkout.poly:33  PL5401 CONFIGURATION_INVARIANT  confirmed-within-stock
  witness: Place@order[0], Place@order[1], Query(order[0]) -> inv, Query(order[1]) -> inv,
           Available(1) -> order[0], Available(1) -> order[1]
```

No per-machine check can see this. The defect lives in the arrival order between machines.

## Principles

0. **The semantics is the definition.** 04-semantics says what a program means; every `poly check` validates the lowering against it.
0a. **One program, three interpreters.** The same machine is checked (all inputs), simulated (sampled inputs, v2) and run (real inputs). Only the environment changes.
0b. **Machines talk only by messages.** Addresses are values, `send` is the only way to affect a peer, and interacting machines are checked together as configurations.
1. **The engines check single machines; poly checks how machines relate.** Safety, governance, simulation and mining stay in the engines. poly's own model checker, poly-ref, checks the lowering, deadlock, liveness and configurations.
2. **The checked program is the running program, over its check domains.** A certificate binds the source, the artefacts and the check results by digest. Out-of-domain inputs are rejected (`strict`) or journaled as drift (`disclosed`).
3. **One source per machine.** Every engine artefact is derived.
4. **No silent clean.** Every check reports clean, findings, refused, underpowered or inconclusive.
5. **No model call on a check or decision path.**
6. **The journal is the corpus.** Runtime journals feed replay, versioning, mining and simulation unchanged.

## Conclusion

The Poly stack already holds the primitives a coding agent needs to write stateful code that holds. poly makes them one language. The first milestone is a lowering that reproduces the field-study results from poly source. The third is an experiment, run before any runtime is built, that measures escaped defects and cost against the host language alone. The runtime work depends on its result.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SAM** | State-Action-Model. The pattern every poly machine lowers to, in its v2 strict profile. |
| **Machine** | A sealed state, a set of actions and one handler per action. The unit of checking and of execution. |
| **Handler** | `on Action { … }`. Requires first, then writes. It either accepts or rejects with a named reason. |
| **Check domain** | The finite set of values a field or parameter takes during checking. Narrower than the runtime type when declared so, and then disclosed. |
| **Invariant** | A predicate on states that holds in every reachable state. |
| **Step property** | A predicate on every accepted step `(pre, action, data, post)`. |
| **Reject property** | A predicate on every step, whatever its verdict. |
| **Path property** | A prefix-closed predicate on the effects emitted along a path, such as `count(k) <= 1`. |
| **Liveness** | A property that something eventually happens, stated with the weak-fairness assumption it needs; its counterexample is a lasso. |
| **Deadlock** | A reachable non-terminal state in which no action is accepted. Checked for every machine. |
| **Checked instance** | The finite set of inputs and states a verdict covers. Every verdict is printed with it. |
| **poly-ref** | poly's model checker: a reference interpreter written from 04-semantics, used for translation validation, deadlock, liveness, configurations and obligation consistency. |
| **Possibility property** | A property that a good path exists (such as a mandate being dischargeable), as opposed to a property of all behaviours. |
| **Trust scope** | The governance scope an instance belongs to. Messages that cross a trust scope pass the gate. |
| **Tagged union** | A type whose values are one of several constructors, each with its own payload. Makes invalid states unrepresentable. |
| **Tri** | The three-valued truth type of policy expressions (true, false, unknown). Machine expressions are `Bool`. |
| **Capability** | An object passed to a handler that grants exactly the authority its effect's labels and targets declare. |
| **Interpretation** | One of three ways to feed the same machine: check (all inputs), simulate (sampled inputs) or run (real inputs). |
| **Embedded surface** | poly written as valid TypeScript with the `poly/embed` combinators; it produces the same AST as the standalone syntax. |
| **Ref** | The address of an instance (`Ref<M>`). It can be stored and passed in messages, but not dereferenced. |
| **Configuration** | A finite set of instances checked together, with messages in transit delivered in any order within a declared bound. |
| **Attached / detached child** | An attached child shares its parent's atomic cascade and kernel shard. A detached child is a separate actor that communicates by messages. |
| **Delivery guarantee** | Every message sent is eventually received: part of the semantics, implemented by the runtime (obligation R1). |
| **Dischargeable** | A mandate is dischargeable when some path reaches its discharge state without a deny under all obligations together. |
| **Kernel assumption** | A property of the runtime (K1 to K8) that a guarantee about running programs depends on. |
| **Witness** | The shortest concrete sequence that violates an invariant or reaches a forbidden region. It can be exported as a trace and as a test. |
| **Effect** | A declared side effect emitted by an accepted step. It carries labels and a class, and passes the gate before it runs. |
| **Label** | A term from a closed vocabulary (for example `egress:external`) that describes what an effect touches. |
| **Obligation** | A rule, machine, invariant or recalled text inside a `policy`, enforced by the Polyaxion gate. |
| **Effect gate** | The Polyaxion guarded merge that decides allow, deny or escalate before an effect or tool call executes. Distinct from the polycheck runtime guard and the polygents gate. |
| **Strict / disclosed** | The two modes of a check domain. `strict` rejects out-of-domain input at dispatch; `disclosed` accepts it and journals it as drift. |
| **Admission** | Passing the check pipeline. Only admitted programs load. |
| **Certificate** | The signed record of what was checked: source digest, artefact digests, check results, domains, stages not run and accepted exceptions. |
| **Ledger** | The signed record of steps, proposals, verdicts, effects, observations and advice, hash-chained per run. |
| **Anchor** | A signed Merkle root over the heads of all runs, published periodically, proving no run was dropped from a period. |
| **Work order** | An effect of a workflow machine, handed to an agent or a person to claim, run and report. |
| **World** | A set of machines, responders and drivers that Polytrion runs against a virtual clock. Deferred to v2. |
| **Lowering** | Compiling a poly construct into the artefact an existing engine reads. |
